signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Disadvantage
signals.text: AUD leads the weekly G10 currency strength board with an average advance of +1.462% across 4 pairs, while USD lags at -0.841% across 9 pairs, opening a 2.302% leader-to-laggard gap. Spot AUD/USD trades at 0.7031, pushing through its SMA20 at 0.6979 but facing steep overhead resistance from its SMA200 at 0.7047 and SMA50 at 0.7080. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net long +44,978 contracts at the 54th percentile, reflecting balanced positioning rather than exhaustion. However, the move runs against an underlying carry deficit where the Fed at 4.00% maintains a 60bp advantage over the RBA at 4.60% on policy rates, while overnight OIS shows SOFR at 3.88% versus AONIA at 4.60% (+72bp favoring AUD). Cross-asset oil volatility from Middle East and Strait of Hormuz developments supports Australian terms of trade, yet upside remains technically capped into the 200-day average. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, momentum-driven against major technical moving average resistance. Catalyst: Fed policy meeting 28 Oct — hike bias priced. Risk: Failure to close above SMA200 at 0.7047 triggers immediate mean-reversion back toward the SMA20 at 0.6979.

signals.title: NZD/USD — CPI Disappointment + ESI Drag
signals.text: New Zealand Q3 CPI printed at 3.7% y/y against consensus expectations of 3.8% and prior 4.1%, while q/q landed at 0.7% versus 1.4% forecast, prompting an immediate drop in NZD/USD to 0.5705. The release deepens New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index to -16.0, the weakest reading in G10 with 13 misses out of 24 prints. Spot remains anchored between its SMA20 at 0.5632 and downward-sloping SMA50 at 0.5769. The Fed-RBNZ policy differential sits at +125bp favoring the US dollar, with the Fed at 4.00% versus RBNZ at 2.75%, while OIS carry offers +113bp for holding USD. CFTC data shows specs net short -11,802 contracts with a sharp WoW reduction of -10,588, leaving the pair exposed as disinflation undermines aggressive RBNZ hike expectations ahead of next week's policy meeting. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD, macro data deterioration reinforcing underlying carry deficit. Catalyst: RBNZ policy meeting 28 Oct — hike bias priced. Risk: A rebound above the SMA50 at 0.5769 invalidates the near-term downside continuation thesis.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew vs Carry Anchor
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.13, holding tightly above its SMA20 at 158.01 and SMA50 at 157.68 within a defined range below the SMA200 at 158.51. The options market displays heavy downside protection demand, with the 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversal printing at -1.86, an extreme put skew that starkly contrasts with the steady spot price action. Meanwhile, the Fed at 4.00% versus BoJ at 1.25% generates a +275bp policy rate cushion, matching SOFR 3.88% versus TONA 1.23% for a +265bp OIS carry advantage to USD. With VIX at 16.7 reflecting normal volatility, broad safe-haven flows remain muted, yet options desks are aggressively paying for downside insurance against verbal or physical intervention heading into the 160.00 psychological threshold. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/JPY, carry support offset by aggressive institutional put buying. Catalyst: Japan Core CPI release today at 23:30 UTC — 1.4% forecast. Risk: A confirmed break above the SMA200 at 158.51 forces a gamma squeeze and tests intervention sensitivity near 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Crowded Spec Short
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1237, pinned below its downward-sloping SMA20 at 1.1263, SMA50 at 1.1459, and SMA200 at 1.1586 in a broader structural downtrend. 1-month ATM implied volatility stands at 6.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.1%, generating an elevated Volatility Risk Premium of +2.5% that reflects significant hedging activity over realized price movement. CFTC positioning highlights crowded speculative short exposure, with Leveraged Funds net short -92,833 contracts at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range (z = -1.78). The carry backdrop remains restrictive for the euro, with the Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% delivering a +135bp spread favoring USD (+144bp on SOFR vs €STR). Elevated option hedging combined with deep speculative short positioning indicates that spot downside momentum is stalling against moving average resistance. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD, downside limited by positioning saturation despite structural carry headwinds. Catalyst: ECB policy meeting 29 Oct — hold bias priced. Risk: A daily close below the 1.1200 handle re-accelerates institutional trend-following selling.
